diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $\sum_{i=1}^\infty a_{i,j}=+\infty$, the operator $C(\{c^{(j)}_i\})$ is unitarily equivalent to the direct sum of a zero operator and the bilateral shift operator on $l^2(\mathbb{Z})$. Otherwise, it is unitarily equivalent to the direct sum of a zero operator and a shift operator acting on a finite-dimensional invariant subspace of dimension at least $2j+1$.
Moreover, the above discussion shows that $\lim_{n_2\rightarrow\infty}\lim_{n_1\rightarrow\infty}\tilde{\Gamma}_{n_2,n_1}(a)=Q(a)$, the required contradiction.

issues.failure_explanation: Each block $C(\{c^{(j)}_i\})$ is a backward shift on the span of basis vectors with value 1. If column $j$ has only finitely many 1's, the block is a finite-dimensional nilpotent shift with spectrum $\{0\}$, not an infinite shift; the inference to '$\spec(A(a))$ is the complex unit disc' is invalid. In fact $\spec(A(a))\subseteq\{0\}\cup\mathbb{T}$ for every $a$, and equals $\{0\}\cup\mathbb{T}$ whenever infinitely many columns have infinitely many 1's, regardless of $Q(a)$. Hence for matrices with infinitely many finite-1 columns and infinitely many infinite-1 columns ($Q(a)=0$), $\mathrm{dist}(1/2,\spec(A(a)))=1/2$ and $\lim\lim\tilde\Gamma_{n_2,n_1}(a)=1\neq 0=Q(a)$: the tower does not compute $Q$, so no contradiction with $\{Q,\Omega_{\mathrm{Mat}},[0,1],\Lambda_{\mathrm{Mat}}\}\notin\Delta_3^G$ is obtained and the lower bound $\mathrm{SCI}=3$ is unproven.

failure_location.quote: Otherwise, for any $N\in\mathbb{N}$, there is a finite-dimensional invariant subspace of dimension at least $N$ upon which $A(a)$ acts as a shift operator. Hence, $\spec(A(a))$ is the complex unit disc in this case.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the embedding so that the $Q(a)\neq1$ case genuinely produces spectra distinguishable from $\{0\}\cup\mathbb{T}$ (e.g., containing eigenvalues off $\{0\}\cup\mathbb{T}$, such as infinite unilateral shifts) while keeping the $Q(a)=1$ case within $\{0\}\cup\mathbb{T}$, and redo the reduction from $Q$.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed optimality results — $\mathrm{SCI}=3$ (not solvable in two limits) for learning $\spec$ and $\spec_{\mathrm{ap}}$ on $\Omega_{\mathbb{N}}$ (thm3 and thm:discrete_space) — are unsupported; the prose claims that thm2's three-limit algorithm is optimal and that 'generically this cannot be achieved in two limits' lose their justification. The $\Pi_3^A$ upper bound is unaffected.
issues.title: False spectral dichotomy in the three-limits lower bound for discrete-space systems
issues.why_classification: The only source-supported route to the advertised optimality result (three limits are necessary) is this reduction, and its central spectral dichotomy is false; a complete resolution requires a new encoding/argument, otherwise the lower bound (a headline guarantee) is abandoned — serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let $F\in\Omega_p$ be the skew product map
$
F(x,y)=(x,y+f(x)),
It follows that there are no eigenfunctions in the subspace $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$.

issues.failure_explanation: All maps in the adversarial family are skew products $F(x,y)=(x,y+f(x))$, which preserve the $x$-coordinate; hence every mean-zero function of $x$ alone is a non-trivial eigenfunction of $\mathcal{K}_F$ with eigenvalue 1, and $\Xi_p^{\mathrm{dec}}(F_{f^{(k)}})=1$ for every member of the family. The construction's alternation requires the odd (strictly increasing $f$) members to have $\Xi_p^{\mathrm{dec}}=0$, which is never the case; the parity argument that produces the SPGA contradiction cannot even be set up. The odd-step value 0 was inferred from Lemma technical_lemma3(a), whose conclusion 'no eigenfunctions in $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$' is false (it only holds for eigenvalues $\lambda\neq 1$; see ISSUE-006).

failure_location.quote: In the above construction, we switched between $\Xi_p^{\mathrm{dec}}(F_{f^{(k)}})=0$ for $k$ odd and $\Xi_p^{\mathrm{dec}}(F_{f^{(k)}})=1$ for $k$ even.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must construct, inside $\Omega_p$, an adversarial family whose odd members are weakly mixing (no non-trivial eigenfunctions) yet agree with the even members on all previously sampled data to the sampled accuracy — e.g., smooth measure-preserving perturbations of a mixing toral map with Lip. constants $\le 2$ — together with a replacement for Lemma technical_lemma3(a), since skew products $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y+f(x))$ always admit the $x$-only eigenfunctions.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound for the decision problem $\Xi_p^{\mathrm{dec}}$ (no algorithms with success probability $>1/2$ deciding existence of non-trivial eigenfunctions in one limit) is unproven, both in thm:torus and in the first claim of main-text thm4, together with the prose that 'no one limit procedure for detecting or computing non-trivial eigenvalues exists'. The $\mathrm{Sp}_{\mathrm{pp}}$ lower bound and the $\Sigma_2$ upper bounds are unaffected.
issues.title: Decision-problem impossibility construction cannot realize the value 0
issues.why_classification: The value 0 is unattainable within the only family the proof constructs, so the root argument fails structurally; a complete resolution requires a new adversarial family and a new phase-transition lemma, otherwise the advertised impossibility for the decision problem is lost — serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Ergodicity can be determined in two limits but not one,
then the SCI of the problem is infinite,

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the Appendix contains an example where determining ergodicity has SCI = infinity. The Appendix's only SCI = infinity result (part (c) of thm:rotation) concerns computing the spectrum on the class of measure-preserving invertible but not necessarily continuous circle maps; ergodicity on the continuous class is classified as $\Pi_2^A$ (two limits), and no result gives SCI = infinity for any ergodicity-decision problem. The prose claims coverage the paper does not provide.

failure_location.quote: Some of these problems are extremely difficult - in the Appendix, we give an example where determining whether a system is ergodic has $\mathrm{SCI}=\infty$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the bullet to cite the actual Appendix result (computing the spectrum after dropping continuity has SCI = infinity), or add a genuine example where deciding ergodicity has SCI = infinity.
issues.overall_effect: The Discussion asserts an unsupported claim about the paper's content, directing readers to a non-existent result in the Appendix.
issues.title: Discussion attributes an ergodicity SCI=infinity example to the Appendix that is not there
issues.why_classification: A local rewording removes the overclaim; no theorem, algorithm, or guarantee is affected — minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: However, the convergence $\lim_{n_1\rightarrow\infty}h_{n_2,n_1}(z,F)=h_{n_2}(z,F)$ need not be monotonic.

Since the sequence $h_{n_2,j}(z,F)$ cannot visit both intervals $I_{n_2}^1(\epsilon)$ and $I_{n_2}^2(\epsilon)$ infinitely often as $n_1\rightarrow\infty$, it follows that the limit $\lim_{n_1\rightarrow\infty}\Gamma_{n_2,n_1}(F)=\Gamma_{n_2}(F)$ exists.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership of $z$ in $\Gamma_{n_2,n_1}(F)$ is decided by the largest index $j$ with $h_{n_2,j}(z,F)\in I^1\cup I^2$. Since $h_{n_2,j}(z,F)\to h_{n_2}(z,F)$ non-monotonically, a point $z$ with limiting value $h_{n_2}(z,F)\ge\epsilon$ (lying in the gap $(\epsilon-1/n_2,\epsilon+1/(2n_2))$, hence outside $\spec_{\mathrm{ap},\epsilon}(\mathcal{K}_F)$) is still declared a member whenever some early iterate fell into $I^1$; so the claimed middle inclusion $\Gamma_{n_2}(F)\subset\{h_{n_2}<\epsilon\}$ fails. Conversely, a point with $h_{n_2}(z,F)<\epsilon-1/(2n_2)$ whose early iterates visited $I^2$ and then converged into the gap is never declared a member, so the lower inclusion fails too. Hence the $\Sigma_2^G$-tower property is not established, and the derived $\Pi_3^G$ classification for $\Xi_{\spec_{\mathrm{ap}}}$ on $\Omega_{\mathcal{X}}$ (used for the third part of thm2) is unsupported as written. (The definition also indexes the test with $j\le n_2$ rather than $j\le n_1$, so the displayed $n_1$-limit is vacuous as written.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Move the second interval to $I_{n_2}^2(\epsilon)=[\epsilon-1/(2n_2),\infty)$ (gap strictly below $\epsilon$), guarantee membership for $\{z: h_{n_2}(z,F)<\epsilon-1/n_2\}$, and define the test over $j\le n_1$; then $\Gamma_{n_2}(F)\subseteq\spec_{\mathrm{ap},\epsilon}(\mathcal{K}_F)$, $\Gamma_{n_2}\uparrow\spec_{\mathrm{ap},\epsilon}$, and all stated classifications follow unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The classifications $\{\Xi_{\spec_{\mathrm{ap},\epsilon}},\Omega_{\mathcal{X}},\dots\}\in\Sigma_2^G$ and $\{\Xi_{\spec_{\mathrm{ap}}},\Omega_{\mathcal{X}},\dots\}\in\Pi_3^G$ in thm:general_koopman_computation, and the third part of thm2 (three limits for general continuous $F$), are unproven as written; the $\Omega_{\mathcal{X}}^\alpha$ and m.p. classifications (Steps 1, 3, 4) are unaffected.
issues.title: Misplaced decision intervals break the Sigma_2 tower for general continuous F
issues.why_classification: A local adjustment of two interval endpoints (plus the index fix) yields a valid tower; every stated conclusion, including the three-limit result for general $F$, survives unchanged — minor.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership of the piecewise affine $F_{c^{(k)}}$ in $\Omega_{[0,1]}^{\delta}$ requires every ratio $a_n=|S_{n+1}|/|S_n|$ to lie in $[1/(1+\delta),1+\delta]$ (both $\|F'\|$ and $\|(F^{-1})'\|$ bounded by $1+\delta$). At each switching index the new ratio equals $\hat r_{k-1}(1-\hat r_k)/(1-\hat r_{k-1})$, which the proof bounds only from above. For example with $\delta=1.5$, $r_1=0.45$, $r_2=0.7$ (satisfying both \cref{deriv_bound} and \cref{sep_bound} for small $\tau>0$), the first switching ratio is $0.45\cdot0.3/0.55\approx0.245<1/(1+\delta)=0.4$, so $\|(F_{c^{(2)}}^{-1})'\|>1+\delta$ and $F_{c^{(2)}}\notin\Omega_{[0,1]}^{\delta}$. The inductively produced family, and the final limit map $F_c$, therefore leave the class whose membership the contradiction argument assumes (via Lemma lem:annulus_phase), and the proof of the lower bound collapses.

failure_location.quote: It follows from the bound \cref{deriv_bound}, that $F_{c^{(2)}}\in \Omega_{[0,1]}^{\delta}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the fixed parameter constraints by also imposing the lower bounds on the switching ratios, e.g. $r_1(1-r_2)/(1-r_1)\ge 1/(1+\delta)$ and $r_2(1-r_1)/(1-r_2)\ge 1/(1+\delta)$, and verify such $r_1,r_2,\tau$ exist for every $\delta>0$ (take $r_1,r_2$ close to 1 with $(1-r_2)/(1-r_1)$ close to 1 and $\tau$ correspondingly small); the construction then remains in $\Omega_{[0,1]}^{\delta}$ and the proof proceeds verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound $\Delta_2^{\mathbb{P}}\not\owns\{\Xi_{\spec_{\mathrm{ap}}},\Omega_{[0,1]}^{\delta},\dots\}$ in thm:interval, and thm1's corresponding impossibility for the smooth Lipschitz class on $[0,1]$, are unproven; the $\Pi_2^A$ upper bound is unaffected.
issues.title: Adversarial interval-exchange maps leave the class Omega_[0,1]^delta
issues.why_classification: The fix only shrinks the admissible parameter region and adds a routine feasibility check; the constructed counterexample family, the annulus alternation, and all stated conclusions survive — minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let $F\in\Omega_p$ be the skew product map
$
F(x,y)=(x,y+f(x)),
For (a), note that the map $F$ is $C^0$ conjugate to $G(x,y)=(x,y+x)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The map $F(x,y)=(x,y+f(x))$ preserves the $x$-coordinate, so every $L^2$ function depending only on $x$ is an eigenfunction of $\mathcal{K}_F$ with eigenvalue 1; any such function with zero mean is a non-trivial eigenfunction in $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$, and its spectral measure is the atom $\delta_1$. Hence both conclusions of part (a) (continuity of all spectral measures on $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$, and absence of eigenfunctions there) are false. The proof's premise is also unsupported: a conjugacy of the natural form $(x,y)\mapsto(h(x),y+u(x))$ would force $f=h$, and $f$ is not a homeomorphism of the torus. The salvageable statement is $\sigma_p(\mathcal{K}_F)=\{1\}$ (via the Fourier decomposition in $y$: $\mathcal{K}_F$ preserves each mode $e^{ijy}$ and multiplies it by $e^{ijf(x)}$, and for strictly increasing $f$ the set $\{x: e^{ijf(x)}=\lambda\}$ has measure zero for $j\ne0$), which is all the $\Xi_p=\{1\}$ steps of the proof of thm:torus actually need.

failure_location.quote: If $f$ is strictly increasing on $[-\pi,0]$, the spectral measure of $\mathcal{K}_F$ with respect to any $g\in L^2(\mathcal{X},\omega)$ is continuous on $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$. It follows that there are no eigenfunctions in the subspace $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace part (a) by the statement $\sigma_p(\mathcal{K}_F)=\{1\}$ and prove it via the Fourier decomposition in $y$ (each mode is preserved and multiplied by $e^{ijf(x)}$, so eigenfunctions for $j\ne0$ would require $e^{ijf(x)}$ constant on a positive-measure set, contradicting strict monotonicity); discontinue the continuity claim for spectral measures on $\mathrm{span}\{1\}^\perp$.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma technical_lemma3(a) is false as stated and must be withdrawn/corrected; the steps of the proof of thm:torus that only use $\Xi_p(F_{f^{(1)}})=\{1\}$ remain valid after the correction, while the decision-problem construction loses its justification (tracked as a separate issue).
issues.title: Skew-product lemma wrongly rules out non-trivial eigenfunctions that exist
